p21_2025_controle_ex1_q1: Q1. Define the concept of class.
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q1_rep: A class is a chunk of code containing variables called attributes and functions called methods from which we control the visibility outside the class and that can be used as a new type of variable. Each method has access and can modify (if not constants) the attributes of the class. Each attribute and method has a visibility which defines if it can be used outside of the class.
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q2: Q2. What is the difference between a class and an instance ?
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q2_rep: A class can define a new type of objects having a behaviour defined by the methods common to all instances of said class. An instance of a class is a variable whose type is defined by its belonging to the class. De plus les méthodes de la classe peuvent être appelées sur l’instance.
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q3: Q3. For variables x1 and x2 of class instances. If we assign x1 = x2, what will be the value of x2 if we modify x1 ?
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q3_rep: The value of x2 will be the same as that of x1 since the objects x1 and x2 are references (in the stack) pointing to the same object (in the heap).
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q4: Q4. How to compare two variables of type String ?
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q4_rep: We only use the method boolean equals(Object obj) to compare two String variables, the operator == only checks addresses and not contents.
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q5: Q5. Give the definition of a simple association. How is this relation represented in UML ?
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q5_rep:
A simple association is present when a class B uses a class A but does not have an instance of class A as an attribute.
In UML, the simple association is represented by a dashed arrow, starting from the using class class, and pointing to the used class. We characterize the type of relation with the given stereotypes : :
  • «call» if the using class calls the methods of the used class
  • «instantiate» if the using class instantiates the used class
  • «uses» if the using class uses the used class as a type (i.e as a parameter in a method)
  • «bind» for the specialization of a type template
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q6: Q6. What is the difference between a controlled exception and a non-controlled exception ? How can we throw a controlled exception ?
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q6_rep: A controlled exception is an exception which has to be catched inside try/catch statement (otherwise the compiler produces an error). They are the exceptions which are instances of Exception without being (by heritage) RunTimeException. When a method potentially throws a controlled exception, it must be indicated in its signature (throws Exception). A non-controlled exception is an exception which is not neccessary catched inside a try/catch statement. They are the exceptions which inherits from RunTimeException. We throw a controlled exception by using the throws new Exception(...) statement.
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q7_rep: When we have an instance of a class which implements an interface stored inside a variable having the type of the interface (abstract type) and we call the a method present in the interface, it is the method implemented in the concrete class which is called. It is what we call polymorphism.
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q8: Q8. What is the difference between the eabstract type and the concrete type of an object ?
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q8_rep: The abstract type is the type given when declaring an object, it is known at compilation and runtime (accessible from the class with .Class). The concrete type is the type given when initializing the object, it is known only at runtime (accessible from an instance with .getClass()).
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q9: Q9. Cite the 4 visibilities in Java and explain them.
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q9_rep:
• private : accessible only from within the class
  • package or package-private : accesible within the same package
  • protected : accessible within the class and its children (by heritage)
  • public : always accessible
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q10: Q10. When defining the du constructor of a child class, how are initializated the private attributes of the parent class ?
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q10_rep: We call the constructor of the parent class in the first line of the child's constructor using super().
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q11_rep: Static methods and attributes are common to an entire class and not to their instances : they can be modified without needing a instance of the class. A static method : does not have access to non-static attributes of the class (but can have access to static attributes of instances of the same class given as parameters of the method); cannot use the this reference.
p21_2025_controle_ex1_q12_rep: A unit test is a test intended to check the good behavior of a unit of a code (usually a function of a class). It should only test one thing at a time ! It also implies that the code has been correctly divided : each class having only one responsability and each method performing only one task.
p21_2025_controle_ex2_uml_enonce_complet: UML : completed (with the addition of class/interface and the relationships)
p21_2025_controle_ex2_q1:
Q1. The getPiece (position : Position) : Piece method of the Echiquier class returns null if no token exists on the given position.
  • - What problem does this create ?
  • - How to avoid it ?
p21_2025_controle_ex2_q1_rep:
• - On risque que l'utilisateur ne teste pas le retour de la méthode correctement et ne propage une valeur null.
  • - We replace the returning of a Piece (that can be void) by an Optional<Piece>.
p21_2025_controle_ex2_q2:
Q2. In the Main class, we want to obtain the colour of a token in this fashion :
Echiquier echiquier = new Echiquier();
Couleur couleur = echiquier.getPiece(new Position(1, 1)).getCouleur();
  • - What are the dependancies of the Main class ?
  • - What is the problem ? (other than the previous one) ?
  • - How to fix it ? What are the new dependancies of Main once fixed ?
p21_2025_controle_ex2_q2_rep:
• Main depends from the Echiquier, Pieces classes and the Couleur enumeration.
  • We call getter on getter; it is an ecapsulation problem.
  • We add a new getCouleur(position : Position) : Optional<Couleur> method in the Echiquier class. It allows us to reduce the dependancies of Main to only Echiquier and Couleur.
p21_2025_controle_ex2_q3: Q3. How to allow a Piece (token) to contain one single ArrayList m_deplacements containing different moves while still being able to call the estValide and realiser method on each element ?
p21_2025_controle_ex2_q3_rep: We can create a Deplacement interface containing both methods and each Deplacement* class can implement it.
p21_2025_controle_ex2_q4: Q4. What is the relatioship of a move class (Deplacement*) towards the Echiquier class ?
p21_2025_controle_ex2_q4_rep: It is a shared aggregate as all tokens (Piece) share the same board (Echiquier).
p21_2025_controle_ex2_q5:
Q5.
  • - What are the responsabilities of the Echiquier class ?
  • -How is it a problem ?
  • - What should be done ?
p21_2025_controle_ex2_q5_rep:
• - The Echiquier class is responsible of the the initialization of tokens (Piece) and their moves on the board.
  • - Having two responsabilities, the Echiquier class violates the unique responsability principle; it creates a problem if we want to reuse the initialization code.
  • - We could create a new class tasked to initialize the tokens with their moves, keeping the Echiquier class with the sole responsability of moving the tokens on the board.
p21_2025_controle_ex3_q1: Q1. Is the heritage proposed relevant ?
p21_2025_controle_ex3_q1_rep: No, as the exception is not present in the parent class. It is a violation of the Liskov substitution principle.
p21_2025_controle_ex3_q2: Q2. Is the heritage proposed relevant ?
p21_2025_controle_ex3_q2_rep: Yes, there is no violation of the Liskov substitution principle.
